title: Periodontitis management and surgical site infection risk in mandibular fracture treatment
html: Aims To assess whether peri-operative periodontal treatment and oral health management in patients presenting with fractured mandibles is associated with a reduction in surgical site infections (SSIs). Methods This was a before-after service evaluation of all patients presenting to the Royal London Hospital Major Trauma Centre with fractured mandibles between January 2021 and January 2023, following the integration of a specialist periodontist and Doctorate of Clinical Dentistry hygiene and therapy students into the outpatient trauma multidisciplinary team. Data were gathered from electronic patient records and radiographic assessments, and compared with a previously published cohort from the same unit (Janaphan et al., 2022; n = 305, 2017–2020). Chi-square analysis and logistic regression with odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals were used. Results A total of 128 patients met the inclusion criteria. SSI occurred in 16 patients (12.5%) in the intervention cohort, compared with 70/305 (22.95%) in the historical cohort (OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.27–0.87; p = 0.014). Stage III and Stage IV periodontal disease was present in 24.2% of the intervention cohort, a higher proportion than in the historical cohort (17.0%). No statistically significant association between severe periodontitis and SSI was identified within the intervention cohort. Conclusions In this before-after service evaluation, the introduction of peri-operative periodontal care and oral health management was associated with a lower SSI rate compared with a historical cohort from the same unit. Causation cannot be inferred from this design. These findings are hypothesis-generating and provide a rationale for a prospective controlled study with multivariable adjustment and standardised intervention documentation.
